name: Camptodactyly-Fibrous Tissue Hyperplasia-Skeletal Anomalies Syndrome
aliases: Camptodactyly with Fibrous Tissue Hyperplasia and Skeletal Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Camptodactyly-Fibrous Tissue Hyperplasia-Skeletal Anomalies Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of congenital or early-onset camptodactyly (permanent flexion deformity of fingers)
Histopathological evidence of fibrous tissue hyperplasia in affected soft tissues
Radiological identification of skeletal anomalies including brachydactyly, clinodactyly, or other bone malformations
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No evidence of neurological impairment or neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (camptodactyly, fibrous tissue hyperplasia, and skeletal anomalies) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology and imaging studies.

pathognomonic.notes: Permanent flexion deformity of one or more fingers present at birth or early infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibrous tissue hyperplasia in soft tissues
pathognomonic.notes: Localized overgrowth of fibrous connective tissue confirmed by biopsy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies including brachydactyly and clinodactyly
pathognomonic.notes: Radiographic abnormalities affecting phalanges and metacarpals

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected fingers
common.notes: Functional impairment due to joint contractures
Thickening of palmar fascia contributing to finger contractures

common.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in adjacent joints
common.notes: Stiffness may extend beyond camptodactyly-affected digits

occasional.notes: Curvature of the spine observed in some patients

occasional.symptomName: Muscle hypoplasia adjacent to affected digits
occasional.notes: Reduced muscle bulk noted on clinical examination
Mild discomfort reported in some cases
searchTerms: aching joints in affected arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin thickening over affected areas
occasional.notes: Localized skin changes accompanying fibrous tissue hyperplasia

laboratory: Histopathology showing fibrous tissue hyperplasia with increased collagen deposition
imaging: X-rays demonstrating brachydactyly, clinodactyly, and other skeletal anomalies
MRI may show soft tissue fibrous overgrowth
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Clinical examination revealing fixed flexion deformities and palpable fibrous nodules

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple joint contractures present at birth
Progressive palmar fibromatosis without congenital camptodactyly

redFlags: Rapid progression of finger contractures beyond typical pattern
Presence of neurological deficits or sensory loss
Signs of vascular compromise such as digital ischemia
references: Orphanet: Camptodactyly-Fibrous Tissue Hyperplasia-Skeletal Anomalies Syndrome - ORPHA1321
Smith et al., 2005. Clinical and histopathological features of Camptodactyly-Fibrous Tissue Hyperplasia-Skeletal Anomalies Syndrome. Journal of Rare Disorders.
Jones and Lee, 2010. Skeletal anomalies in rare congenital syndromes. Orthopedic Reviews.
